findings.description: async retry_any.__ror__ flattens `other` when it is an instance of retry_all, but the check should be for retry_any. `retry_all | retry_any` therefore loses the AND semantics of the retry_all operand.
findings.rationale: Trigger: `(a & b) | async_retry_any(c, d)`. The code splices `other.retries` (a, b) into retry_any(a, b, c, d), turning `(a and b) or c or d` into `a or b or c or d`. The retry decision becomes silently wrong.

findings.description: async retry_all.__rand__ flattens when other is a retry_all, which is correct. It does not handle the sync/async mix the type hints allow, but that is not a clear defect.
findings.rationale: Low confidence that this is a real bug.
